acceptanceItems.requirement: Responsive UI performance, soak, and capacity require the dedicated performance campaign.
acceptanceItems.deferReason: Performance and soak execution is a later dedicated milestone after runtime evidence.

acceptanceItems.requirement: Persistence P1-P7 evidence is collected only through the dedicated published persistence campaign.
acceptanceItems.deferReason: The Phase 10 command explicitly excludes persistence runtime execution.

acceptanceItems.requirement: ESC has no gameplay meaning.
Q closes only the top context and never cascades.
E confirms only the current semantic action.
Left selection/default preview, right capability table, and middle-drag orbit keep distinct meanings.
Default action, movement, attack, and interaction are previewed before execution.
Unavailable authorized actions are disabled with viewer-safe reasons; unperceived actions are hidden without placeholders or counts.
Actions preserve valid selection and never force turn recenter.
Pending, denied, stale, awaiting-projection, and reconciled states remain distinct.
An open context table blocks the world default left action while camera controls remain usable.
Exploration uses the base shell without initiative or End Turn controls.
Encounter adds initiative, resources, and End Turn without replacing the base shell.
Turn, resource, and End Turn state comes from authoritative projection.
Observer HUD stays viewer-safe and exposes no player authority.
Player persistent Minimap, separate Player Map, and Objective Tracker are forbidden rather than required.
Inventory and equipment use projection and authorized transfer intents.
Hidden and private items expose neither placeholders nor counts.
Journal reading, navigation, and private create/edit intent follow projection permissions without requiring a separate Player Map.
Accent, UI scale, text scale, action rows, delays, motion, and reset use the preference boundary.
Supported binding conflicts are presented safely and never create gameplay authority.
